title: Slimline SDK: credential-swap + pullstream unification (Python/TS/Go)
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Compact credential-swap hook and unified pullstream adapter across Python/TS/Go SDKs; ergonomic API for stream consumers; improved retry windows and small perf optimizations. Bumps Python/TS/Go SDK minor versions.
description:
Motivation: engineers have been juggling slightly different streaming handshake primitives and credential refresh hooks in each SDK, which complicates upstream demos and increases maintenance surface. This PR introduces a slim, explicit credential-swap hook and a compact PullStream facade that aligns Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs around a single small surface area. Goals: reduce allocation churn on reconnect, make credential handoff deterministic, and provide an ergonomic pull-based stream consumer that maps easily to async/iter/observables in each language.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced CredSwap interface (language idiomatic): Python: CredSwapCallable, TS: CredSwapProvider, Go: CredSwapFunc. The implementation surface is intentionally tiny: single async/sync call to exchange an expiring token for a live token + optional metadata.
- Added PullStream adapter that sits on top of existing stream sockets and exposes a consistent next()/close() contract (Python async iterator / TS AsyncIterable / Go channel-based iterator wrapper).
- Centralized retry profiles used for streaming reconnects (short, medium, long) and added a deterministic jitter scheme to reduce thundering restarts.
- Minor runtime perf: avoid copying byte buffers on reconnect in the TS/Go adapters; reuse existing KV cache slice on session handoff when compatible.
- Docs and examples: updated quickstarts in each SDK and the redwood/examples/streaming demo to show cross-language parity.
